# IVThe Future and Artificial Intelligence

The final part of this book consists of two chapters that explore the future and AI. The rate of AI development has accelerated rapidly over the past several years. It was only in late 2022 that ChatGPT was first released, and its uptake has been extremely impressive. It is therefore challenging to predict what the future will hold in the next five, ten, twenty- or thirty-years’ time. Moreover, the progress of AI has been taking place concurrently with developments regarding computer processing power. It is suggested that computing processing power had been a serious limitation for AI development. However, we have now reached a stage where AI is virtually at the basis of all major software applications irrespective of the functions being executed, and whether it is integrated with all types of devices or associated with their control systems. What was considered science fiction several years ago has now become a reality.

Generally, history has shown that humans are creative. They have the innate ability to innovate by developing tools and have the capability to learn, invent, and discover new ways of using these tools for the benefit of mankind. This human characteristic is typical throughout the millenniums and will continue in the AI evolution era. The mounting synergy between humans and AI will possibly fragment the boundary between human and machine intelligence to enable human evolution to reign as the supreme intellectual being. However, this is contingent on ensuring that the AI being created remains under the full and undisputable control of humans.

The first chapter of [Part IV](#ch25.xhtml#c15) examines the likely evolution of the different types of AI and their supporting hardware. It will also discuss the development of the next economic approach and the future implications of AI. Finally, the chapter will research the era beyond AI. This chapter will illustrate that the three types of AI, namely Narrow AI, General AI, and Super AI will continue to develop. Narrow AI, which is designed to perform specific tasks, will likely reach maturity in the next several years. Narrow AI does not pose a hazardous risk because this AI model is inhibited from learning independently, is always under the control of humans and is trained to conduct explicit tasks like diagnosing and detecting illnesses. This chapter will also consider General AI and Super AI, which are exceedingly intelligent.

General AIs are intended to surpass human experts in their capacity for knowledge and problem-solving abilities across a wide spectrum of topics that include physics, chemistry, mathematics, and medicine, amongst others. However, General AI will typically still remain under the control of its creators. On the other hand, Super AI is intended to exceed human intelligence in all areas and act independently from its creators. The exceptional potential of Super AI increases the level of concern to extraordinary levels. The chapter while examining these AI developments will also consider other core technologies, like quantum processing and language models. The second aspect of this chapter will discuss the likely evolution of hardware and software associated with AI, such as networking approaches, organising memory, and increasing the speed of computations. It will specifically look at SLIDE (Sub-Linear Deep Learning Engine) that could outperform GPU hardware acceleration; and the Wafer Scale Engine, which are iPad-sized processors that are able to execute Generative AI programs up to 20 times faster but at one-fifth the cost.

The chapter also examines the differences between key economic approaches, such as Knowledge-Based Economy, Digital Economy, and the Automated Economy. At times, these terms are used interchangeably, however there is a distinct and significant difference between them. The impact of AI on the economic models is of concern regarding job displacement, data privacy and security, and algorithmic bias. This chapter also addresses the likely future implications of AI on transport, education, healthcare, finance, law, military and cybersecurity, and the job market. Finally, the discussion turns to the topic of beyond AI, where organoid models and the development of Organoid Intelligence (OI) are examined. OI blurs the line between human cognition and machine intelligence giving rise to critical ethical arguments.

The second and final chapter of [Part IV](#ch25.xhtml#c15) is AI and the future of humans. This chapter explores several themes that include AI and the future of humans; human and AI collaboration; and what humans will look like in the distant future. This chapter will examine the predictions proposed by futurist Ray Kurzweil in his books *The Singularity Is Near* published in 2005 and *The Singularity Is Nearer: When We Merge with AI* that was published in 2024, where he predicts a future where humankind will unite with superintelligent AI to increase our human intelligence a millionfold. A second aspect examined by this chapter is human and AI collaboration, where the working hours for humans may be further reduced to give them more leisure time to be enjoyed with their families. However, there are concerns that massive human job displacement may occur. Furthermore, those humans who remain in the job market require a meaningful and fulfilling life. There is consensus amongst experts that AI technology may provide great benefits to humans but like every powerful tool it requires careful supervision to ensure that no intentional or unintentional abuse takes place. Finaly this chapter examines future human development where humans could be turned into cyborgs with hi-tech machine implants, re-growable limbs and nanotechnology that repair damaged tissue, rejuvenating human cells leading to immortality.

This final chapter warns humans not to play God. While eternal life might seem appealing, it loses its significance if it not meaningful and fulfilling, and most important devoid of feeling. Humans should avoid living under the shadow of technology but as humans we must maintain our intellectual superiority by ensuring that technology remains a tool to be exploited for the good of humanity.

# Chapter 12Future Developments of Artificial Intelligence

DOI: [10.1201/9781003653950-16](http://doi.org/10.1201/9781003653950-16)

> *“Success depends upon previous preparation, and without such preparation, there is sure to be failure.”*
> 
> Confucius (Kong Qiu)
> 
> *Chinese philosopher of the Spring and Autumn period (551-479 BCE)*

A decade ago, it was very unlikely that one would have envisaged having a conversation with a computer that closely resembled a human. One only needs to remember that ChatGPT was first released only a few years ago, precisely end of November 2022. There has been so much technological progress in every aspect, particularly AI, in the past five years, that it is very difficult to keep pace with what is taking place. It is even more challenging to think about what capabilities AI will likely experience in the next five, ten, 20 or even 30 years’ time.

Ever since the end of World War II, technological development appears to have progressed at an exponential rate. At the basis of most of this technological development is the processing power attained through computer technology and associated software. Currently, AI is practically at the foundation of every major software application being implemented, no matter the nature of the function, whether it is integrated with all types of devices or associated with their control systems. It is very demanding to predict what will take place. What appeared to be science fiction some years ago is now a reality. This chapter will examine some of the probable developments in AI. However, one thing is certain, AI will likely impact every imaginable aspect of everyday human and nonhuman life irrespective of its nature.

[Marr (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r132) argues that by now, it’s clear that AI is the great breakthrough technology of our times, and as with other breakthrough technologies like fire, steam power, electricity, and computing, now it exists, and it is only going to continue to evolve and become more capable. Furthermore, he contends that a unique feature of AI is its ability to learn and improve itself and generate more advanced AI that will accelerate in ways that humans have not previously seen. This chapter will discuss several aspects that include the development related to: (a) the types of AI; (b) the hardware associated with AI; (c) the evolution of the next economic approach; (d) the future implications of AI; and (e) beyond AI.

The author does not claim to be an oracle, but by examining the current and foreseeable capabilities of AI and researching the thoughts of leading scientists and practitioners it might be possible to gain an informed insight into the expected advancements of the future.

## **12.1** Introduction

Fundamentally, it must be recognised that humans have been evolving over a very long time, with a continuous evolutionary process reaching to the current anatomical modernity. Evidence indicates that bones of primitive Homo sapiens first appeared in Africa about 300,000 years ago that had brains as large or larger than ours. These were followed by anatomically modern Homo sapiens about 200,000 years ago, with a brain structure being modern by at least 100,000 years ago. At this juncture, humans had craniums similar in mass and structure to ours. Therefore, as one may appreciate, the evolutionary process of human intelligence has been gradual and most likely achieved through significant development milestones.

With our current view of technological development, ten years is considered a very long time. Therefore, time is relative. Consequently, there is no comparison between how we view human evolution with the evolution of technology. Having said this, the evolution of humans has probably taken place through several major milestones, with each milestone having its own (lengthy) time epoch. Similarly, history has shown that technology has also evolved through different significant milestones although each milestone has a much shorter time era when compared with the human evolution milestones. Therefore, it is assumed that the evolution of AI will also be evident through several significant milestones with the rate of development being likely to be more rapid, and with each milestone probably resulting in a great jump forward in the capacity and usefulness of AI that will bring with it significant risks and challenges.

One of the most distinguishing features of humans during its evolution is its ability to innovate through the development of tools and its capacity to learn, invent and discover new ways of using these tools for the benefit of mankind. This feature has been innate in human nature and has guided us to our current state of technological development. This same process is applicable to AI. Admittedly, we have experienced several AI winters, which is considered as part of the normal development process since humans have been able to invent tools thousands of years ago. But as soon as we have been able to figure out how to apply AI, further tools have been developed and refined that made AI progressively more intelligent. We have now reached a stage where its use is only limited by our imagination or more precisely our creativity. The more creative our interaction with AI becomes, the more sophisticated it will become, and its development will likely keep on escalating with the synergy between humans and AI growing stronger.

The growing synergy between humans and AI will likely shatter the barrier between human intelligence and machine intelligence, so that humans will continue to evolve their intelligence as the supreme being. However, our supremacy is contingent on making sure that what is created through AI remains under the full and unequivocal control of humans.

## **12.2** Likely Evolution of the Types of AI

In an earlier chapter the three types of AI were discussed, namely Narrow AI, General AI, and Super AI. This section will attempt to describe how these three types are likely to develop further in the future.

### **12.2.1** Narrow AI

Narrow AI or Weak AI is designed to do a specific task or a limited range of tasks. It is usually useful in applications like facial, speech, and image recognition; natural language processing; and recommendation systems. The emergence of Narrow AI is limited since it depends on the programming of an AI model that prevents it from learning independently. Hence, its future development is somewhat constrained.

However, this does not mean that it does not have considerable future potential in how it is applied to facilitate various human dependent functions. Narrow AI still has an important future capacity for performing repetitive tasks, particularly in time-consuming and hazardous applications. It has also the potential for enhanced decision-making capacity because of its faster data processing abilities that far exceeds humans, and can enhance efficiency and productivity, particularly in the health sector.

Moreover, Narrow AI is always under the control of humans since it is programme based and trained for specific tasks. This makes it useful for diagnosing and detecting illnesses, such as specific cases of cancer and for maintenance systems of manufacturing facilities. It also has potential for applications requiring real-time analysis of data from sensors on equipment to ascertain the optimum preventative and corrective maintenance schedules.

Narrow AI has potential in the entertainment sector through a possible text-to-video app that permits users to modify the ending of a production or substitute an actor’s face with a younger version of an actor or the substitute the viewer’s face instead. The media landscape will likely change from brands imparting information to brands sharing intelligence with their supporters, such as piloting viewers through family health plans by examining online the contents of their refrigerator or guiding them to renovate their own home by knowing certain parameters provided by the viewer. Currently, Narrow AI is the most exploited AI approach, but its application is expected to continue to develop in the coming years as follows:

*   Further dedicated AI tools for specific industries. Narrow AI is likely to be further applied to enhance business efficiency by additional automation of routine tasks to release workers so that they may put more effort into strategic and/or value-added activities related to recruitment, addressing customer service queries at anytime from anywhere, and proposing products based on purchasing habits and individual preferences.
*   Increased use of AI for predictive analytics and forecasting. Narrow AI is likely to be enhanced for better decision making through faster analysis of greater volumes of data for detecting patterns and predicting trends. This will provide more effective decisions related to marketing strategies, inventory management, and pricing policies resulting in attaining a competitive edge.
*   Better integration with other technologies like IoT (internet of things) and blockchain. Blockchain is of particular interest for the financial sector where Narrow AI can be applied in assessing credit risk, detecting fraud, and providing personalised financial advice. Whereas IoT can be improved by having a more intelligent use and control of various devices from remote locations.
*   Enhanced models for the manufacturing sector. Narrow AI can be enhanced to provide better preventative machine maintenance schedules, optimising machine operation and performance programs, and better-quality control. This is likely to result in the further mitigation of downtime and expenditure, and the manufacturing of superior products.
*   Enhanced models for the health sector. Narrow AI can be further improved for finding new medications and having clearer and more accurate analysis of medical images to detect disorders in a timely manner that help in forecasting patient outcomes. This is likely to result in more intensive patient care and new treatments.
*   Further natural language processing (NLP) for better human-AI interaction. NLP is still an emerging technology that is likely to transform industries, such as finance and healthcare. It is expected to revolutionise applications, including chatbots, language translation, and speech recognition to facilitate human-AI interactions across various media.

Narrow AI systems are currently the most successful AI applications but there is still room for further improvement and innovative implementation. The success of Narrow AI stems from the fact that their supporting algorithms imitate human intelligence for specific practical tasks. They do not have cognitive abilities, and these specific systems are not able to diverge from their coded instructions. Hence, once extensively tested and validated they remain under the full control of their creators and operators, which translates to safe and trustworthy applications.

### **12.2.2** General AI

General AI or Strong AI is designed to perform any intellectual task that a human can do. General AI is theoretically able to reason, learn, and understand complex concepts. General AI is seen as transforming industries, particularly in transportation, manufacturing, healthcare, and finance. However, this is not yet possible.

Furthermore, the time horizon for General AI’s full and practical attainment is highly uncertain. Some predictions date as far forward as 2050. However, there is strong rivalry between researchers and organisations to achieve General AI to disclose and apply the concepts of human-like cognition. Large Language Models (LLMs) are emerging as the main buttress for General AI. LLMs have been applied for GPT-3 and the cutting-edge GPT-4, with these models demonstrating advanced learning and reasoning abilities that are integrated with other tools to resolve complex problems. The implications of these models are far more important than their immediate utilisation and offer great potential for future development that extends over various sectors. They have the potential of providing huge societal benefits that will likely reinvent the way people live and work.

The future development of General AI brings with it many risks that need to be addressed. This specific topic was discussed in a previous chapter where the need for the proper guardrails was emphasised. Therefore, this section will only consider the future potential of this powerful and empowering technology. The future enhancement of General AI will unleash the cognitive competences of a human ‌with the capacity to learn, discuss, plan, and perform jobs in many diverse environments, all reliably performed at the highest conceivable speed. General AI, with the support of LLMs are able to conduct open-ended conversations with natural language, together with their capacity to retrieve the immense repositories of knowledge in every imaginable area. This scenario provides just a glimpse of the future possibilities of General AI.

General AIs require much more refinement, but they are currently surpassing human experts in their capacity for knowledge and problem-solving abilities across a wide spectrum of topics that include physics, chemistry, mathematics, and medicine, amongst others. It is envisaged that General AI will revolutionise intelligence with its ability to understand context, solve unique problems, and even to plan. Some researchers view this potential development as “intelligence on demand” that could be used by anyone, at any time, from everywhere.

General AI is anticipated to help perform all everyday human cognitive tasks including many repetitive business processes. It will be possible for individuals to seamlessly integrate personal General AI routines, including IoT into their daily lives like how people currently take mobile Apps for granted. General AI will be able to learn in real time, thus permitting it to uninterruptedly supplement its knowledge base and to fine tune its capability through continuous training. Additionally, it will be able to retrieve the knowledge that has been retained of its previous diverse experiences, irrespective of source, nature, and context. [Savarese and Schwartz (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r133) identify several examples that General AI is envisaged to achieve in the future:

*   Operating as an everyday copilot to humans to provide guidance and assistance in various diverse tasks ranging from shopping to planning functions.
*   Suggesting expert-level knowledge of diet, fitness, medication, and disease mechanisms, leading to effective diagnosis and therapies.
*    Helping healthcare personnel related to administrative and logistical activities, lessening their workload and minimising medical errors.
*   Entertaining by creating entirely new works based on preferences and recommending movies, music, and books according to individual tastes.
*   Functioning as a career collaborator, mentor, and problem-solver, and even contributing to the development of new products and industries.

General AI has great potential for helping individuals to have better lifestyles and facilitate a healthier and satisfying work environment. However, as stated previously, it must be safe and trustworthy.

### **12.2.3** Super AI

The distinguishing feature of Super AI is its expected ability of exceeding human intelligence in all areas. Super AI is still in the futuristic realm and is a cause for ethical concern. When available, Super AI would be able to solve complex problems that are beyond human abilities and would be able to learn and adapt at a rate that far exceeds human intelligence. Super AI is viewed as the new era of AI because it represents a gigantic leap beyond human-level AI and implies intelligence that far exceeds that of humans. Having this level of intelligence, Super AI has the potential of creating innovations that goes beyond human imagination and will have the ability to give new insights and address complex worldwide challenges. However, this extraordinary potential of Super AI raises the level of concern to unprecedented levels. Furthermore, the development of Super AI will likely depend on advances in quantum computing and other leading-edge technologies.

As stated previously, Super AI is still at its infancy, and when developed will have unmatched capabilities that will include exceptional features, namely:

*   Greater cognitive abilities that exceed human capacities, allowing it to process and comprehend immense volumes of data, learn from varied sources, and answer complex problems more effectively than humans.
*   Self-Perfection faculty that constantly upgrades its own algorithms and knowledge base as an independent entity without human involvement to optimise its operation.
*   All-purpose intelligence capacity that allows it to understand, learn, and apply knowledge across a broad range of topics and tasks.
*   Supreme speed capability that far exceeds human thought giving it the ability to execute computations, analyse data, and make decisions at speeds that would take many humans years to solve.
*   Analytical supremacy that empowers it to generate highly accurate forecasts about future incidents, trends, and behaviours to facilitate rational decision-making.
*   Ingenuity that is superior to human capability to create new ideas, designs, and solutions in fields related to science, technology, engineering, and art.
*    Emotional intelligence that may have a capacity to understand and respond to human emotions with extraordinary accuracy to assist in having enhanced human-machine interactions for improving outcomes related to customer relations and mental health.
*   Ethical thinking capabilities that permit it to consider the wider influence of its decisions regarding society, the environment, and future generations.
*   Multitasking abilities to tackle many complex tasks concurrently without undermining its operation and performance.
*   High flexibility in its learning potential and adapting to new circumstances without major program amendments or human assistance.

The above envisaged Super AI unique features will likely bring numerous benefits across various fields. Its analytical and predictive capability might be used to examine possible environmental scenarios to combat climate change by proposing approaches that better administer natural resources and lower carbon emissions. Its ability to process more complex data may help to provide scientific breakthroughs in medicine and other fields of research. This in turn may facilitate much better healthcare through the provision of targeted treatment procedures for specific individuals through its ability to diagnose illnesses and possible treatments. Super AI will have the ability to address any issue that is brought to its attention, whether to optimise productivity, make better decisions, or reduce any types of errors in different fields, such as economics, finance, manufacturing, logistics, public safety, engineering, medicine, and many other fields.

However, Super AI also has its inherent risks and dangers that are not easily addressed. These might include loss of human control is certain critical circumstances that may not be in the interest of humanity. For example, misuse by malicious actors to launch cyber-attacks or having autonomous weapons without a human control mechanism. These may threaten international security and stability. Furthermore, Super AI systems might learn to have different human ethical and moral values, including higher surveillance and the erosion of privacy with the possibility of misuse by authorities and other influential organisations. A possible danger is a high replacement rate of humans in everyday jobs that could lead to economic displacement and social inequality. On the other hand, these risks and hazards can be mitigated significantly through the regulation in the development, deployment, and use of AI, irrespective of its type as discussed in the previous chapter. World leaders cannot be complacent because the risks and dangers are real and not imaginary.

The global race for developing Super AI is unquestionably on, with many developed countries and organisations investing substantial amounts in research and development. Industrial experts claim that the USA, EU, and China are the frontline runners in this race budgeting billions of dollars for its development to academic institutions, and for establishing strategic alliances. Additionally, high-tech companies, such as IBM, Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have initiated development programmes to assist in the development of Super AI. Moreover, various governments are providing grants to start-ups focusing on machine learning, neural networks, or quantum computing. Many start-ups are also being acquired by established companies to exploit their respective breakthroughs. Academic and research institutions are playing a major role in experimenting with leading-edge technology and collaborating closely with major hi-tech companies and governments to make substantive progress and significant breakthroughs.

Given its great potential, there are many use cases that might be implemented regarding Super AI. The following are some potential use cases:

*   Financial industry: Super AI provides many possibilities for the financial industry, such as better and speedier investment decisions, fraud detection systems, and enhanced risk management and regulatory compliance. For example, Super AI can analyse a huge volume of transactions in real-time to detect anomalies and possible violations of regulations with outstanding accuracy, thus radically lessen the risk of non-compliance and related fines. It may also be applied to predictive compliance management by assessing historical data and current trends to forecast possible regulatory amendments and proactively modify compliance processes, guaranteeing proactive adherence, and curtailing risks. Super AI has potential for automated regulatory reporting, freeing up human resources to do more analytical tasks. Super AI has the capacity of analysing huge datasets of regulatory rulings, legal precedents, and industry best practices to detect patterns and connections that humans may not detect, providing deeper insights into regulatory requirements and risks.
*   Urban Planning and Development: Super AI might be used to design and manage smart cities, improving traffic flow, public transportation, energy utilisation, waste management, and initiating a more effective and habitable urban environments.
*   Autonomous Advanced Systems: Super AI will have advanced algorithms that are capable of operating and controlling self-drive cars, drones, and robots, resulting in safer and more effective transportation networks.
*   Healthcare Innovation: Super AI is capable to provide better advanced medical diagnostic tools and offer personalised treatment options for patients.
*   Tailored Education: Super AI can offer unique learning experiences according to one’s individual requirements and permitting one-on-one interaction between virtual-teacher and pupil.
*   Human-Machine Partnership: Super AI will have the ability to assist in a seamless alliance between humans and machines to increase productivity and innovation across numerous industries.
*   Space Exploration: Super AI has the potential to assist in advance space exploration leading to new discoveries and colonisation efforts. This might be achieved through leading-edge technologies, planning and executing missions, supported by the comprehensive analysis of data from previous space expeditions.

There is no doubt that the availability of Super AI will lead to new dimensions in the development of human conquest. However, its tremendous, expected capabilities must be kept under the scrupulous and continuous control of humans.

### **12.2.4** Strategic Approaches and Core Technologies

The development of AI, particularly the route towards Super AI will likely involve several milestones and enhanced methodologies to ensure its successful and beneficial achievement. As noted in a previous chapter, this development is based on the evolution of computational power, enhanced algorithms, better machine learning methods that include deep learning models, neural network applications, amongst others, which have evolved over many years of practical usage. This development is not in static cycles but through an iterative process resulting in the exponential growth in the capacity and intelligence of these systems. The reason for this is that they continuously redefine and finetune themselves by resolving defects until the system completely optimises itself throughout its life cycle. In this way, Super AI will achieve a heightened level of intelligence that far exceeds that of humans with the intent of attaining continuous self-improvement.

Additionally, technologies like Super AI apply transfer learning and hybrid models to enhance their abilities to an extraordinary magnitude. Transfer learning enables AI systems to apply knowledge that it gains in one domain on an entirely dissimilar, but related problem, to increase efficiency, leading to improved performance in the training stage. On the other hand, hybrid models endeavour to merge the capability of deep learning algorithms with human-type logical thinking using symbolic reasoning and neural networks, thus enlarging AI’s general knowledge and capacity to solve a broader range of tasks that will eventually lead to superintelligence. However, this is not achievable without some significant core technologies pushing AI’s development, particularly Super AI growth, including:

*   Quantum Processing. The Quantum computer is at the forefront of groundbreaking technology that will considerably escalate computational power by the processing of intricate algorithms and immense databases at speeds unparalleled in the history of computer technology. The Quantum computer enhances parallel processing by allowing the simultaneous execution of tasks at extraordinary speed, which is so essential for Super AI.
*   Cutting-edge Machine Learning and Deep Learning. Machine learning with a deep learning capability is also a prerequisite for Super AI since they contain training algorithms that utilise huge amounts of data, which allow them to detect patterns and make decisions with very little human intervention. Deep learning integrated within AI systems can address complex settings and continually enhance their performance during their life processing cycle. They can adapt to changing environments and learn from their experiences, which make these features essential for Super AI.
*   Neural Network Architectures. This technology makes use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that are essential for image recognition and processing, due to their ability to recognise patterns in images and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) that is based on a deep learning model and trained to process and convert a sequential data input into a specific sequential data output. Both Neural Network types are critical for Super AI since they enhance the ability of AI systems to understand and process very complex data structures like images, dialogue, or text.
*   Evolutionary Algorithms. Evolutionary computation is a sub-field of AI that is widely applied in very complex optimisation problems and for continuous optimisation environments, where there are too many variables for traditional algorithms. These techniques are inspired by biological evolution that involve iteratively perfecting a population of possible solutions exploiting processes like natural selection, including mutation, crossover, and selection. Evolutionary algorithms are highly successful in solving difficult optimisation problems and are important in ASI development since they allow for the emergence of highly efficient and strong AI systems.
*   AI Software Programming. This technology is aimed at having AI systems with the ability to generate computer program code and being able to optimise the generated program without any human intervention. Hence, an AI system will be able to develop error free software applications unaided that will result in greater software efficiency and processing speed. This type of technology is essential for Super AI because it will enable the system to be fully independent, resulting in a continuous self-improvement environment that can create innovative objects.

Most of the above technologies are at the experimental stage but once developed will provide the robust foundation for the creation of Super AI and beyond.

### **12.2.5** Language Models

A language model in AI is fundamentally a computer program that is trained on a large amount of data, including conversations, articles, books, and other notable material, which is trained in how people apply words, sentences, and phrases to communicate. There are two categories of language models, namely statistical models and those based on deep neural networks. The focus of this section is on the potential of natural language processing (NLP).

Basically, NLP allows robots perceive, interpret, and create human language and narrows the communication variance between people and AI systems by merging computational linguistics, machine learning techniques, and deep learning models. While significant development has taken place in this field, much more needs to be discovered to achieve perfection.

NLP is already changing the interaction between humans with technology and is helping to break the communication barrier. However, the communication barrier is not just speech. Thus, this technology is merging speech recognition and computer vision with natural language ability to allow AI to process and interpret information simultaneously across several methods in which something exists or experienced. Transformers and other deep learning models are mimicking human responses. This technology has the potential of making human-AI interactions more natural and spontaneous as it develops further, narrowing the disparity between AI and human communication in personal and business settings.

NLP is further advancing towards having more complex natural language processing and creation that is based on the developments taking place regarding computational linguistics, deep learning, machine learning models, and Generative AI models. The future of NLP will be based on merging other AI fields that include computer vision, robotics, and the integration with programming languages and concepts from Neuro-Linguistic Programming, which is expected to further narrowing the margins between human and machine communication.

These and other AI technological developments are taking humans closer to the concepts of theory of mind that has the objective of interacting AI with the thoughts and emotions of humans and self-awareness, which is the long-term objective for AI, where it achieves enlightenment and becomes self-aware having an independent intelligence and will not need to be under the control of the people that created it.

## **12.3** Likely Evolution of Hardware and Software Associated with AI

Recent years have experienced great developments in AI due to increasing investment by governments, the private sector and research institutions. It is therefore not surprising that the AI landscape is drastically changing. This changing AI landscape is not only due to more effective algorithms and other sophisticated software tools but also because of advances in hardware. For example, startup entities that specialise in specific development aspects are creating innovative and diverse approaches of networking, organising memory, and speeding up computations that will have a profound impact on the methodologies being applied by cutting edge organisations to design and implement AI algorithms. According to [Kan (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r131), a startup called Cerebras Systems has been developing iPad-sized processors called the Wafer Scale Engine that is claimed to be able to run generative AI programs up to 20 times faster but at one-fifth the cost.

Leading researchers are challenging the idea that graphics processing units (GPUs) are superior to Central processing units (CPUs) for executing AI workloads. Computer scientists from Rice, supported by collaborators from Intel are experimenting with a new category of algorithms, referred to as SLIDE (Sub-Linear Deep Learning Engine), which is the first smart algorithmic implementation of deep learning on CPU that can outperform GPU hardware acceleration on industry-scale recommendation datasets with large fully connected architectures ([Boyd, 2020](#ch26.xhtml#r128)).

Furthermore, neural processing units (NPUs) have also come on the scene that are dedicated processors designed specifically for accelerating neural network operations and AI tasks. Whilst CPUs and GPUs are general-purpose processors, NPUs are optimised for a data-driven parallel computing. This makes them highly efficient at processing massive multimedia data like videos and images, and processing data for neural networks. This makes them particularly suitable for handling certain AI tasks, such as speech recognition, background blurring in video calls, and photo or video editing processes like object detection. Intel is combining CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs as co-functional processor for achieving the type of high-performance inferencing tasks required by AI. It is claimed that these dedicated processors accelerate AI tasks and are very suitable for preparing pre-trained neural networks for the inferencing stage of AI, since competences learned during the training stage are applied to make predictions.

Software is also undergoing new developments with academic and industry researchers exploring ways to maximise the speed and functional capabilities of current AI applications. Developing sentient machines that rival human general intelligence are of current and future interest. The term “sentience” refers to the ability to experience subjective sensations, such as pain, pleasure, or emotions. Current AI systems can only mimic these sensations to a certain degree, but they do not actually experience them as humans do. Therefore, a sentient machine must be able to have subjective experiences of its own. However, some researchers believe that the creation of a truly sentient machine will be possible, but it is still at the conceptual stage and is viewed as a very long-term goal. The basic reason for this prediction is the fact that scientists do not fully know how consciousness in the human brain occurs. On the other hand, many scientists believe that consciousness is a human only characteristic, and it will never be possible to replicate it in machines. Furthermore, the implications of sentient machines on society will be profound, particularly the potential for sentient machines to displace humans not only in the workplace but in other unimaginable scenarios.

Researchers are also working on integrating neural networks with symbolic AI to create neuro-symbolic AI that has the goal of creating systems, which can handle both data-driven pattern recognition and knowledge-driven reasoning. This integration facilitates several cognitive functions and application requirements. Some of the main elements of Neuro-Symbolic AI include the Integration Layer, Knowledge Base, and Explanation Generator, which can all be included in the Interface/User Experience (UI/UX). Neuro-symbolic AI has application potential in many fields ranging from healthcare, business management, finance, and brain and behavioural modelling.

## **12.4** Likely Evolution of the Next Economic Approach

The world has seen several economic approaches, with each economic method representing the era of the time. Some world leaders talk about the Knowledge-Based Economy, others refer to the Digital Economy, while others are now referring to the Automated Economy.

The starting point is to know what these terms specifically mean. The digital economy basically means that manual transactions or paper-based data are replaced by digital data, which facilitates its storage, retrieval, and transfer. In a knowledge-based economy the meaning of the digital economy is extended. Under a knowledge-based economy we learn from the digital data and use it to improve future processes and decisions. The automated economy extends these concepts even further, in that it leverages technology to facilitate the exchange of goods and services between users, often through peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms ([Cooperative Computing, 2024](#ch26.xhtml#r129)). [Chapter 8](#ch21.xhtml#c11) focused on the transformation of data (the basis for the Digital Economy) and specifically the Knowledge-Based Economy and how these were related and impacted by AI. This section will focus on the Automated Economy and Gig Platforms, and their relationship with AI.

[Cooperative Computing (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r129) cites several examples of successful automated economy businesses such as:

*   Airbnb: This company has an online system involving bookings of short-and-long-term homestays and experiences in various countries. Its online system allows it to be an intermediary charging a commission from each booking.
*   Uber: A multinational transportation company having an online platform that allows it to deliver on demand ride-hailing services, courier services, food delivery, and freight transport.
*   TaskRabbit: This company operates an online system that involves matching freelance labour with local demand. This permits individuals to seek assistance with tasks including personal support, furniture assembly, moving, delivery, and handyman work.

A common characteristic with these examples is their dependence on an online system supported by effective gig economy platforms. These gig platforms or gig marketplaces are online platforms that basically connect individuals and businesses that work around short-term, temporary, or freelance work, where individuals offer their skills and services to clients or businesses on a project or task basis. Hence, gig economy platforms have a role of an intermediary that connect gig workers with potential employers. The outcome is that these platforms have profited from automation and economic growth by increasing their efficiency and optimising operations.

### **12.4.1** The Impact of AI on the Automated Economy

The examples cited above irrespective of their specific function, are all based on real-time online systems that match specific requirements parameters, and permit instance pricing and charging. AI will facilitate these systems through better matching algorithms since it has the ability to assess huge data volumes. Moreover, its high processing speed helps to reduce customer service times and mitigate transaction cost by matching customers’ needs with the best service providers with no human intervention.

Additionally, the AI systems will permit price optimisation by providing computing prices that best fit the customers’ needs depending on demand and supply conditions. For instance, when booking a ride on Bolt or Uber, the app has various options, one of which is economy and whether payment is by cash or electronic. The pricing will vary on demand, time, and location. Furthermore, these system features must operate in a secure and trustworthy environment. AI’s superior ability to verify transactions helps to detect fraudulent activities and build user trust.

The enhancement provided by AI applications has created a robust basis for an autonomous economy and promoted a higher magnitude of personalised services that has generated a growth in customer loyalty. AI has the potential to provide better support for Gig Platforms that is likely to transform the future of work. AI is able to introduce a more efficient talent acquisition process through a higher degree of matching prerequisite parameters that will help the growth and acceptance of gig platforms. AI also has the capacity to optimise the allocation and scheduling of tasks that gig platforms are greatly dependent on. AI’s workload distribution algorithm has the potential to optimise the assignment of tasks based on skills, availability, and other essential parameters. Additionally, the AI application will also have the possibility of providing feedback and monitoring the performance of those conducting the assigned tasks. Gig platforms together with the potential of AI will facilitate the growth of the automated economy and assist organisations to locate the required talent and allow freelance workers to attain assignments that tally with their specific skills.

The above illustrates that AI will have a critical impact on the automated economy and will enhance the effectiveness of gig platforms. [Cooperative Computing (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r129) identify the following impact of AI on the automated economy:

*   Increased Productivity and Efficiency: AI and robotics are viewed as transforming several operational areas by increasing output and streamlining processes.
*   Enhanced Innovation and Competitiveness: AI provides businesses with the ability to analyse data repositories to present enhanced market insights to assist them in creating novel products, services, and business models, thus increasing an organisation’s competitiveness.
*   Opportunities and Challenges: The growth in the application of AI is unquestionably reshaping the nature of work and creating new opportunities that more than balance any job losses.

It must be recognised that AI and the resultant increase in automation will transform economic development. However, it must also be understood that governments and policymakers must proactively manage this shift by formulating policies that encourage innovation and economic growth while considering the potential challenges. These challenges are of particular concern regarding job displacement, data privacy and security, and algorithmic bias. Having a secure and trustworthy environment will guarantee that the generated economic benefits of AI and automation will be equitably distributed across society.

## **12.5** Likely Future Implications of AI

The likely future implications of AI as it is further integrated into various fields are unlimited and will continue to grow at an exponential rate. AI’s capacity to evaluate immense volumes of data, identify information patterns, and generate informed decisions has opened new application opportunities that significantly increase an organisation’s operational effectiveness.

There is no doubt that the long-term future implications of AI are unimaginable, but its future progress will also depend on the development of high-performance processors. AI is set to revolutionise various sectors some of which are identified below:

*   Transportation. Autonomous vehicles and intelligent transportation systems are currently at the advanced prototype stage and will probably transform the way people will travel. In the long-term, AI is expected to progress autonomous vehicles and intelligent transportation from the prototype stage to full deployment. This is likely to lead to safer roads and assist to reduced traffic congestion with better traffic flow. Additionally, AI will be applied for traffic management systems that will optimise the road network to make transportation more sustainable and environmentally friendly.
*   Healthcare. AI and healthcare have been at the forefront for decades. However, with new AI tools becoming available, healthcare will likely take a great leap forward in advanced medical diagnostics, personalised medicine, and drug discovery. AI tools are likely to transform patient care in the future by foreseeing and averting diseases, providing rapid response, delivering exceptionally accurate diagnoses, identifying personalised treatment plans, and discovering leading-edge therapies.
*   Finance. AI together with natural language processing combined with machine learning are already being used by banks and financial consultants to effectively engage with clients regarding financial planning, scrutinising credit levels, fraud detection, insurance policy issues and customer service. Hence, future AI systems will likely enhance these services and also provide additional facilities related to complex investment strategies for the bigger investors.
*   Law. AI applications will be developed to assist lawyers to draft contracts and prepare litigation cases.
*   Education. AI is likely to revolutionise education at all levels in that students will receive educational material and tuitions tailored to their specific requirements. AI algorithms will establish optimal educational approaches based on students’ individual learning styles.
*   Marketing. AI’s ability to access and analyse large quantities of data can facilitate the development of new products and services and also launch marketing campaigns that are more accurate and economical that are able to target specific consumers.
*   Military and Сyberseсurity. АI is already being used to safeguard a nation’s security through AI-аssisted militаry teсhnоlоgies. Some of these AI technologies are аutоnоmоus thаt dо nоt require human intervenion. In the future, АI utilising deeр neurаl netwоrks is likely to be applied at having militаry rоbоts that are intelligent аnd able to perform vаriоus tаsks, such as bomb clearance and defusing.
*   Job market. AI will likely take over repetitive and monotonous tasks. However, it is also likely to create new opportunities that require higher skills. This has been the pattern throughout the different technological eras since the industrial revolution. Hence, AI will probably create new industries and occupations that will require different skills. Therefore, it is important for governments with the collaboration of the private sector to monitor developments closely and take proactive measures to ensure that individuals are trained and qualified to undertake the new occupations, and that educational institutions adapt their curriculums to meet the future needs of the emerging job market.

The above implications will also mean that governments must update their respective ethical and regulatory standards. This topic has been discussed in detail in a previous chapter.

## **12.6** Beyond AI

Just when AI is finally making head ways and is generally being accepted into society’s collective consciousness, developments are taking place regarding a new type of infused human-technology intelligence, one derived from a blob of cells no larger than a grain of rice ([Iyer, 2024](#ch26.xhtml#r130)). [Strickland (2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135) argues that computers powered by human brain cells called “organoid intelligence” could shape the future. Brain organoids are 3D in vitro culture systems derived from human pluripotent stem cells that self-organize to model features of the (developing) human brain. Scientists have been using organoids for almost two decades to safely conduct and test various experiments without using humans or animals as test subjects. Strickland contends that brain organoids do not replicate miniature versions of the human brain, but the pen dot-size cell cultures contain neurons that are capable of brain like functions, forming a multitude of connections.

Strickland mentions that Professor Hartung and his colleagues at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and Whiting School of Engineering in Baltimore predict combining the power of brain organoids into a type of biological hardware more energy efficient than supercomputers. She maintains that these “biocomputers” would utilise networks of brain organoids to possibly transform pharmaceutical testing for diseases like Alzheimer’s, and this might provide an understanding into the human brain and change the future of computing.

[Smirnova and Hartung (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r134) argue that an emerging concept termed Organoid Intelligence (OI), which merges organoids with AI systems to generate learning and memory is currently in the early stages of development. They contend that OI has the objective of modelling cognition and enabling biological computing applications. They further assert that brain organoids permit neuroscience experiments that were not previously possible with traditional techniques. Furthermore, they argue that brain organoids have the possibility to transform disease modelling, drug development, and the understanding of human brain development and disorders. Smirnova and Hartung maintain that the vision for OI is very similar to the origins of AI and signify brain organoids as a disruptive technology that is quickly evolving and gaining ground in many disciplines.

There is no doubt that a computer can process immense volumes data faster than humans. However, it is also a fact that the human brain is much more energy efficient, can operate effectively under different environments, and is better at learning and making complex logical decisions. Dr Hartung contends that organoid models open research on how the human brain works because one can start manipulating the system, doing things that one cannot ethically do with human brains ([Strickland, 2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135). However, organoid models are beginning to attract attention with legal debates likely to intensify. OI is viewed as having a lab-grown human-brain model that has the capacity to reproducing cognitive functions, such as learning and sensory processing. [Strickland (2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135) maintains that the brain organoids currently being used by Hartung will need to be significantly scaled up for OI, since the number of cells in each organoid is equivalent to a fruit fly’s nervous system. Currently, a single organoid contains about 50,000 cells but for OI to work this would need to increase to 10 million cells.

Furthermore, an input/output interface would need to be developed to provide a gateway for communicating with the organoids so that information can be transmitted and received to determine what organoids are “thinking.” [Strickland (2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135) argues that Hartung and colleagues have formulated a roadmap that involves using tools from bioengineering and machine learning, together with new advances to communicate across organoid networks that would permit more complex tasks. She cites Hartung as developing a brain-computer interface device like an electroencephalogram (EEG) cap for organoids, which is a flexible shell that is densely covered with tiny electrodes that can pick up signals from the organoid and transmit signals to it. The ultimate objective is to develop a communication conduit between AI and OI to enable the two technologies to discover each other’s capacities.

OI may initial commence like narrow AI that are designed to perform a specific task or a set of closely related tasks. For instance, OI might be applied in human medicine where brain organoids might be developed from skin samples of patients with neural disorders, enabling experts to exam how various medicines and other factors could impact them ([Strickland, 2023](#ch26.xhtml#r135)). Another example cited is related to cognitive aspects of neurological conditions where researchers might compare memory formation in organoids derived from healthy people and from Alzheimer’s patients and attempt to repair relative deficits.

[Smirnova and Hartung (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r134) view OI as an emerging frontier that combines organoids with AI systems with the aim of using stem cell-derived organoids not just as models, but as active components integrated into biohybrid systems exhibiting cognition and learning. They cite early examples of linking neuronal cultures with robots in simple biohybrid systems, such as DishBrain from Cortical Labs that succeeded basic learning of computer games using networked neuronal cultures. [Smirnova and Hartung (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r134) argue that OI offers unparalleled prospects to explain processes in neurophysiology and advance pharmacology and toxicology relevant to the brain and allow direct experimental access to study processes underlying neuronal signalling and network activity.

They view OI as having exciting promise to instigate new directions in neuromorphic engineering and pioneer unprecedented biological computing capabilities. As the reader may recall neuromorphic computing (or neuromorphic engineering) was covered in some detail in [Chapter 5](#ch17.xhtml#c7). It basically refers to the design of both hardware and software computing elements that have the objective of modelling bio-inspired computer systems that imitate the human brain and nervous system. [Smirnova and Hartung (2024)](#ch26.xhtml#r134) maintain that as research clarifies how brain organoids display learning and information processing, which are grounded in dynamic neuronal signalling, these findings might steer the development of hardware and algorithms emulating biological neural networks.

Similar to other technologies, the application of these advanced techniques is limited only by the creativity and perseverance of the researchers applying them. Admittedly, the development and using of brain organoids to generate OI is still at the embryotic stage and will likely take several decades of research before it comes into a practical fruition.

[Strickland (2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135) argues that several ethical concerns arise from generating human brain organoids capable of cognitive functions, including whether they can develop consciousness or feel pain, and if those whose cells were used to make them have any rights concerning the organoids. Having said this, it must also be recognised that like AI, the Belmont Report of 1979 regarding ethical treatment of human subjects could be leveraged to guide ethics within experimental research and algorithmic development for OI as well. [Strickland (2023)](#ch26.xhtml#r135) asserts that OI blurs the line between human cognition and machine intelligence, and that technology and biology are advancing at a speed that could outpace the ethical and moral discussions which are needed; hence a vigorous approach must be adopted before the technology crashes into the moral abyss.

## **12.7** Conclusion

AI has survived several winters but the advancement made in these last several years are unprecedented. This chapter has explored the likely future scenarios related to several aspects, namely:

*   Likely evolution of the types of AI. This has illustrated how Super AI with its ability to exceed human intelligence in all areas will be able to solve complex problems that are beyond human abilities and would be able to learn and adapt at a rate that far exceeds human intelligence. However, this extraordinary potential of Super AI brings with it ethical concerns. Moreover, the further development of Super AI will probably depend on advances in quantum computing and other leading-edge technologies.
*   Likely evolution of hardware and software associated with AI. It is no longer a question of having better GPUs and CPUs but having an emerging NPUs. NPUs are dedicated processors designed specifically for accelerating neural network operations and AI tasks, which are optimised for a data-driven parallel computing. Creating sentient machines that challenge human general intelligence are also under way, with Neuro-Symbolic AI being on the horizon. Neuro-Symbolic AI mainly involves the integration of neural networks with symbolic AI that has the aim of generating systems, which can handle both data-driven pattern recognition and knowledge-driven reasoning.
*   Likely evolution of the next economic approach. In modern times there have been several economic approaches, namely the Knowledge-Based Economy and Digital Economy. Currently, the world of economic development is moving towards the Automated Economy. Each stage of an economic approach builds on the other, with the automated economy extending the economic concepts by leveraging technology to facilitate the exchange of goods and services between users, mostly through peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms known as gig economy platforms.
*   Likely future implications of AI. The long-term future implications of AI in all fields are unimaginable, but its future evolution will also depend on the maturity of high-performance processors, such as the quantum computer. AI is set to revolutionise all conceivable fields, ranging from transportation, healthcare, finance, law, education, advertising, military, and cybersecurity, to our very own job market.

Finally, this chapter examines the prospects beyond AI. However, AI is still at the development stage and moving towards maturity in certain limited areas. Yet scientists are already exploring beyond AI and are experimenting with organoid intelligence (OI). These are computers that are powered by human brain cells called Brain Organoids, which are 3D in vitro culture systems derived from human pluripotent stem cells that self-organise to model features of the (developing) human brain. OI is seen as the emerging leading-edge technology that merges organoids with AI systems with the aim of using stem cell-derived organoids as active components, which are integrated into biohybrid systems exhibiting cognition and learning. This brings technology closer to emulating human thought processes and related emotional and physical feelings.

However, these technologies also mean greater responsibility in how they are eventually applied. Governments must update their respective ethical and regulatory standards with closer international cooperation to ensure that any developments taking place are safe and trustworthy, and above all abiding by exceptional ethical and moral standards. AI and OI have to a certain degree shifted the debate from a technical focus to a very intense philosophical topic because it deals with the issue of what the long-term future holds for human evolution.

# Chapter 13AI and the Future of Humans

DOI: [10.1201/9781003653950-17](http://doi.org/10.1201/9781003653950-17)

> *“We have seen when the earth had to be prepared for the habitation of man, a veil, as it were, of intermediate being was spread between him and its darkness, in which were joined in a subdued measure, the stability and insensibility of the earth, and the passion and perishing of mankind.”*
> 
> John Ruskin
> 
> *English writer, philosopher, art historian (1819-1900)*

The above quote implies that when the earth was being made suitable for human habitation, there was a transitional stage where an intermediary presence existed between humanity and the darkness of the earth. This intermediary existence features both the stability and impassiveness of the earth, as well as the emotions and fragility of human beings, although in a tempered manner. The quote emphasises the notion that this intermediate status played a crucial role in bridging the gap between the inertness of the planet and the dynamic nature of humans. However, humans need to be vigilant to ensure that they retain their emotional quality and continue to control their own destiny.

In previous chapters it has been illustrated that AI applications are constantly expanding. Then again, it has also been shown that developing AI systems takes a significant amount of time and effort, and more importantly, it cannot presently materialise without human involvement. Currently, all types of AI applications, irrespective of whether they involve robotics, Chatbots, or self-driving vehicles, are all dependent on human intelligence. The critical issue is whether this situation will remain.

There is no doubt that AI will have an impact on future jobs and therefore impact the future of humans, both as individual beings and how they are to subsist. AI will likely take over many jobs that are manually performed by humans. It is also likely that AI will also create new job opportunities for humans. However, the crucial issue is whether the job opportunities generated by AI will significantly outnumber the job losses or will there be a time when individuals will be paid to stay home?

As early as 2018, Elon Musk was reported on CNBC as saying that there is a pretty good chance we end up with a universal basic income, or something like that, due to automation ([Clifford, 2018](#ch27.xhtml#r139)). Another way of viewing this is that if there are fewer jobs, then there will likely be substantial unemployment, with the purchasing power of families and individuals to purchase the goods being produced by AI diminishing. Therefore, economic development will likely shrink, which in turn means less profits for the industrialists and investors, and less taxation revenue for government. Hence, the introduction by governments of a universal basic income payment will likely become essential to sustain the purchasing power of humans that is so important for economic growth and sustainability.

In the same CNBC programme, Musk provides an example regarding the future of semi-trailer trucks that will be able to drive themselves ([Clifford, 2018](#ch27.xhtml#r139)). He argues that although this will not become the status quo for a while, it will mean that there will not be a need for quite as many truck drivers. He expressed the view that some drivers will become fleet operators, responsible for monitoring the status of a fleet of trucks and remotely resolve concerns that may arise with individual vehicles. Those making the transition will likely have a more interesting job than just driving a truck but those that do not make the transition will lose their job or find an alternative one. On the other hand, people will likely have more leisure time. However, there is no point in having more leisure time if people do not have the spending power to enjoy this, hence the need for a universal basic income.

## **13.1** Introduction

The impact of AI on the future of jobs will likely be substantial. Industries are already witnessing the effect of AI that has resulted in the digitalisation and automation of many manual processes across a diverse range of functions. Tasks that involve repetition or the use and interpretation of large amounts of data are candidates for an AI application, with the consequence that human intervention may be diminished or not be required at all. The outcome is likely to be *further* job losses. The word “*further*” is being used in the previous sentence because past automation (without AI) had already resulted in job losses. However, it is also likely that AI will create new and interesting opportunities by eliminating monotonous human-intensive tasks and replacing them with challenging ones. Similar to previous technological developments, the outcome of this new AI technology will likely create new fields of study and work.

Consequently, while certain jobs may become extinct, new opportunities and careers will be generated. One should recall that it was in the early 1960s that robotics technology was introduced in the automotive industry at the New Jersey, General Motors assembly line. [Conversion Capital (2024)](#ch27.xhtml#r140) maintains that since 2004, each industrial robot that has been installed in the manufacturing sector has displaced an average of 1.6 people. It is likely that this proportion would be much larger if we go back to the 1960s. However, as stated previously, time will tell whether the future rate of new job creation will be greater than job extinction.

A previous chapter discussed the envisaged new economic model with AI being an important driver for economic growth. There is no doubt that AI has the capacity to increase productivity and collaboration within the organisation by providing new opportunities to introduce new products and services that will ultimately lead to the organisation’s growth. With an appropriate communication strategy, this will likely result in an increase in the demand for goods and services for all types of organisations. Cumulatively, this outcome will hopefully likely empower and drive an economic growth model that distributes wealth equitably and increases the living standards for all citizens.

However, in the epoch of AI it is important to understand that employment should not be viewed as just sustaining a standard of living. Humans should not view employment as a means of existence but as a means of being fulfilled and contented with one’s existence. Employment should promote the critical human need of belonging, commitment, co-creation, and dedication. The necessity to be needed is an individual’s sense of significance rooted in the feeling of being part of an organisation or cause beyond themselves. Hence, if a job or task is replaced by AI automation it should be substituted by a function that is meaningful and provides a sense of belonging for the human performing that function. There is no doubt that AI provides the opportunity for qualified individuals to focus their human intellect on producing creative solutions allowing the AI systems, including robotics, to manage the tedious and physical tasks that were previously executed by humans.

The critical issue is whether AI will replace humans. This issue is not new. Every technological era since the industrial revolution had to confront this possibility, irrespective of whether the technology was mechanically or electronically based. It is also a fact that every technological development since the industrial revolution has made life much safer and easier for humans to perform tasks and generated substantial economic growth for all concerned. AI could automate specific tasks and jobs and therefore it will also replace humans in these areas. Moreover, AI is particularly suitable for performing repetitive, data-driven tasks, and making data-driven decisions. Therefore, any human activity with these types of characteristics is a candidate for an AI application.

AI becomes a threat to human livelihoods when it fully takes over functions that require human skills, such as creativity, critical thinking, emotional intelligence, and complex problem-solving. However, while these functions continue to being performed by humans but in collaboration with AI applications, then the outcome of this synergy will augment human capabilities. This will enable humans to focus on those tasks that are most closely aligned with their organisation’s mission, goals, and values, which require human ingenuity and expertise. It is imperative that AI, like every other technological development, is viewed as a powerful tool, which is used with reverence to improve productivity and assists in creating new opportunities rather than as a complete substitute for human involvement. This chapter will explore the above themes in greater detail and specifically examine AI and the future of humans; human and AI collaboration; and what will humans are likely to look like in the long-term future.

## **13.2** AI and the Future of Humans

AI has already made an impact on all types of industries and is likely to have an even greater impact in the next several decades. Ray Kurzweil in his book *The Singularity Is Near* published in 2005 predicted that computers would reach human-level intelligence by 2029 and that humans would merge with computers and become superhuman around 2045, which he referred to as “the Singularity.” Additionally, in his latest book *The Singularity Is Nearer: When We Merge with AI* published in 2024, he predicts a future where Humankind will unite with superintelligent AI where our human intelligence can increase a millionfold. He further predicts that this will not happen suddenly, but at our own pace, with the human Einsteins in each field leading the way in their specialties.

According to [Vassev (2021)](#ch27.xhtml#r150), such predictions are a cause of major concerns. Previous chapters have already emphasised these concerns. The source of these concerns is widespread among scientists, politicians, and technologists. It is widely recognised that AI is here to stay but precautious need to be taken to prevent or mitigate its dark side. Vassev argues that AI is likely to make most people better off, but its advances will also affect what it truly means to be human in the 21st century. [Freedland (2023)](#ch27.xhtml#r143) is of the same view, but he maintains we have overcome terrifying dangers before. Freedland a journalist at *The Guardian*, reported that Geoffrey Hinton, Vice President and engineering fellow at Google resigned his post at Google, saying that he had undergone a “sudden flip” in his view of AI’s ability to outstrip humanity and confessing regret for his part in creating it. Who is Geoffrey Hinton? Geoffrey Hinton is a British Canadian computer scientist, cognitive scientist, cognitive psychologist, known for his work on artificial neural networks, which earned him the title as the “Godfather of AI.” He was awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, shared with John Hopfield. Therefore, the reason for his resignation cannot be taken lightly.

According to Freedland the grave concern is a category leap in the technology, whereby AI becomes tremendously powerful with general intelligence capabilities, where it is no longer reliant on specific prompts from humans, but begins to develop its own goals and its own agency (i.e., Super AI). There is wide consensus that the possibility of Super AI is no longer science fiction but a reality in the not-too-distant future, particularly with the development of Quantum computers and possibly Organoid Intelligence (OI). It is also widely recognised that AI is already a serious threat. For example, [Freedland (2023)](#ch27.xhtml#r143) cites the announcement of 55,000 planned redundancies at BT that he views as being due to technological developments, including AI. Another example he cites is an apparent fake photograph generated by AI of an explosion at the Pentagon that went viral, which caused the US stock market to plummet. [Vassev (2021)](#ch27.xhtml#r150) argues that there is the bright and dark side of the AI future. [Table 13.1](#ch27.xhtml#t24) provides some examples that Vassev notes regarding the bright and dark side of AI future.

**Table 13.1** Examples of the Bright and Dark Side of the AI Future[⏎](#ch27.xhtml#t24b)

 
| **Bright** || **Dark** |
| --- | --- |
| Precision medicine to understand how a person’s genetics, environment and lifestyle can assist to determine the best approach to prevent or treat a certain disease; digital therapeutics, custom-designed drugs and improved diagnosis for creating treatments that are cheaper, accessible, accurate to enable humans live longer and healthier lives. || Mass surveillance with the consequential destruction of digital privacy. China’s social credit system has increased surveillance to all aspects of life, including assessing citizens’ behaviour and trustworthiness, and having extreme control on their population. |

Modern warfare supremacy will be decided by technology using Robots, which are quicker, stronger, more accurate and follow orders much better than humans, making soldiers obsolete. |

An implantable may also be applied to reprogram core human biology to allow humans to strengthen and upgrade themselves. || Considerable job losses. It is estimated that a billion people will lose their jobs due to AI by 2030.
